battle.name: 朱燮起義
battle.brief: 大業九年七月，吳郡崑山縣博士朱燮率學生起兵，與毗陵管崇合眾七萬，響應楊玄感，共推餘杭劉元進為天子、朱燮任僕射；十二月攻丹陽敗於隋將吐萬緒，管崇歿於黃山，朱燮與劉元進再攻吳郡兵敗戰死。卡面秦連弩屬戰國舊物，此役城守所倚仍是床弩、弩砲與投石。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 大業九年（613）江南這場起義，交戰的兩方是起義眾與隋朝官軍。起義一方以餘杭劉元進、吳郡朱燮、毗陵管崇三支兵馬為主：劉元進於七月先起於餘杭，朱燮以崑山縣博士之身份率數十學生起於吳郡，管崇起於毗陵，三路互為聲援，旬月之間眾至數萬；其後朱燮與管崇所部合流，擁眾七萬，共推劉元進為天子，朱燮與管崇並任僕射。毗陵、東陽、會稽、建安一帶的起義隨之接應，起義眾多為抗役逃兵、逃戶與鄉里壯丁，編制鬆散，供應靠沿途徵發與鄉民接濟，並無常備軍籍。官軍一方是隋朝中央與江南地方郡兵：煬帝在楊玄感於黎陽起兵、隋軍主力西征之際，遣左屯衛大將軍吐萬緒與光祿大夫魚俱羅率各郡兵下江南鎮壓；吳郡、丹陽等重鎮由郡兵與城防軍把守，兵力多為臨時徵發的鄉兵，後又令江都郡丞王世充發江南兵數萬渡江直攻吳郡。吳、會一帶是隋的漕運與賦稅核心，郡兵雖多而戰備空虛，官府對鄉里的控制只剩稅簿與徵役兩端，於是義軍得以在郡縣之間迅速擴張。
countriesEn: This rising of 613 in Jiangnan was fought between the insurgents and the armies of the Sui dynasty. The insurgent side was composed of three main bodies: Liu Yuanjin of Yuhang, Zhu Xie of Wu Commandery and Guan Chong of Piling. Liu Yuanjin rose first, in the seventh month; Zhu Xie, a county school official, rose with a few dozen of his students in Wu; Guan Chong rose at Piling. The three supported one another, and within a month their crowds had grown to tens of thousands. Zhu Xie and Guan Chong then merged their forces, mustering seventy thousand men, and together they raised Liu Yuanjin to the position of emperor, themselves taking the two posts of ministerial servants. Piling, Dongyang, Kuaiji and Jian'an answered the call in turn. The rank and file of the rising consisted chiefly of conscripts who had fled the corvée, run-away households and local able-bodied men. Their organisation was loose, their supply was drawn on the spot from the villages that sheltered them, and they had no standing roster. On the government side stood the Sui court together with the militia of the southern commanderies. While Yang Xiangan was raising revolt at Liyang and the main Sui army was held in the north, Emperor Yang sent the Left Commandery Protector General Tu Wanzu and the Director of the Palace Table of Ceremonial Fish Julu down into Jiangnan to suppress the rising. The heavy towns of Wu and Danyang were held by locally conscripted militia and city garrisons; later the deputy prefect of Jiangdu, Wang Shichong, was ordered to take several tens of thousands of Jiangnan troops across the river in a direct march against Wu. Wu and Kuaiji were the granary and the tax base of the Sui empire. The militia were numerous, but their war footing was hollow: the court's grip on the countryside had shrunk to the tax registers and the levy, and that was why the insurgents could spread from one commandery to the next so quickly.
people: 朱燮是這場起義的發起者之一，吳郡人，早年出家為道士，通經史、習兵法，隋時任崑山縣博士，是江南少數既通曉經術又熟悉兵法的學官；起義時他只率數十名學生響應，卻以「民苦役者，赴之為歸」為號召，把逃役的士卒與抗役的鄉戶收攏起來，隨後與毗陵的管崇合兵，共推劉元進為主，自己與管崇同任僕射；十二月攻丹陽失利後與劉元進退保建安，再攻吳郡時戰死。管崇是毗陵義軍的首領，與朱燮合流後兵力最厚，是朱燮最可靠的同盟者，大業九年十二月在黃山被隋將吐萬緒斬殺。劉元進為餘杭人，少時好俠義，起兵最早，七月響應楊玄感，旬月眾至數萬，因北方的楊玄感迅速敗亡而放棄渡江北上；他被朱燮、管崇共推為天子，成了起義眾名義上的領袖，兵敗後與朱燮同歿於吳郡。官軍方面，左屯衛大將軍吐萬緒與光祿大夫魚俱羅奉詔鎮壓江南，吐萬緒在丹陽大破義軍，於黃山斬管崇；江都郡丞王世充則以發兵渡江、銳進吳郡的手腕收場，迫得劉元進、朱燮兵敗，三萬餘降卒被坑殺於黃亭澗。背景中的楊玄感於七月在黎陽起兵反隋，數十日即敗亡，卻把隋朝西征的大軍牽制在北方，為江南起義打開了時間窗口。
peopleEn: Zhu Xie was one of the men who set this rising in motion. A native of Wu Commandery, he had been a Taoist priest in his youth, had read the classics and histories and studied the art of war, and in Sui times he held the post of school official at Kunshan County. He was one of the few learned men in Jiangnan who knew both the literature of the schools and the business of war. When he rose he took only a few dozen students with him, yet he rallied the fugitives from the corvée and the peasantry of Wu with the call that those wearied by forced labour would find in him a way home. He then joined forces with Guan Chong of Piling, and the two together raised Liu Yuanjin to be their leader, taking the posts of ministerial servants themselves. After the defeat at Danyang in the twelfth month he and Liu Yuanjin fell back to Jian'an, and he was killed when they attacked Wu once more. Guan Chong was the leader of the Piling insurgents. After the merger his command was the strongest of the three, and he was Zhu Xie's most dependable partner; in the twelfth month of the ninth year of Daye he was cut down at Huangshan by the Sui general Tu Wanzu. Liu Yuanjin was a native of Yuhang, given to chivalry from boyhood, and rose earliest of the three: in the seventh month he answered Yang Xiangan's revolt and drew tens of thousands within a month, and gave up the plan of crossing the river northward only because Yang Xiangan was crushed so quickly. Zhu Xie and Guan Chong pushed him forward as emperor, and he became the nominal head of the insurgents; he died with Zhu Xie at Wu when the rising was destroyed. On the government side, the Left Commandery Protector General Tu Wanzu and the Director of the Palace Table of Ceremonial Fish Julu were sent down into Jiangnan by imperial order; Tu Wanzu broke the insurgents at Danyang and beheaded Guan Chong at Huangshan. The deputy prefect of Jiangdu, Wang Shichong, closed the affair by leading Jiangnan troops across the river in a sharp march on Wu, breaking Liu Yuanjin and Zhu Xie and putting more than thirty thousand surrendered men to death in Huangting Brook. In the background, Yang Xiangan had raised revolt at Liyang in the seventh month and was crushed within a few dozen days, but he pinned the Sui expeditionary army in the north and so opened the window of opportunity for the rising in Jiangnan.
kits: 卡面上的兵器是秦連弩，即以弩機儲力、一踏一發的連發弩：把拉力的一部分存進弩機，踩下板機便可連續射出多支矢。連弩的做法在中國出現得極早，戰國時已屬大型床子弩，《墨子·備高臨》記「連弩之車」，《六韜·虎韜·軍用》記「絞車連弩」，戰國楚墓亦有連弩實物出土；秦弩機的形制延續到漢以後，連發的原理則一直散在民間器械與床弩之中。放到大業九年的江南，這件兵器卻不屬於義軍的裝備：起義眾自吳郡、毗陵集合，多用弓、矛、盾、柴刀一類的舊式器械，攻城靠雲梯與穴地，守城靠人眾與城頭的弓弩；官軍同樣沒有連發弩可用，吳郡、丹陽城頭架的是床弩與弩砲，配合拒馬、鹿角、擂木與投石機，攻城方則以巢車、撞車、穴車與火箭對付。真正把這類連發射擊用成軍械的，是隋唐之後的諸葛連弩，明人《天工開物》論其「機巧雖工，然其力綿甚，所及二十餘步而已，此民家防竊具，非軍國器」，《武備志》則說東南人喜用而力輕，一弩連發十矢，懦夫閨婦皆可執以環守其城——正好說明這張卡面講的「守城一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外」在技術上做得到，在隋末的實戰中卻仍停留在器物層面，沒有成為大隊作戰的依靠。江南水網縱橫，義軍與官軍的補給多靠船，隋軍由江都發兵渡江，義軍則沿吳淞、浙東水道北撤建安、再折返吳郡。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Qin repeating crossbow, a crossbow that stores part of the pull in the trigger mechanism so that a single stroke of the tread releases a whole string of bolts in succession. The idea is of great antiquity in China: by the Warring States period the repeating crossbow was already a large bed-mounted weapon, the Mohist text Mozi on the Defence of High Positions records a 'cart with repeating crossbows', the Six Secret Teachings of the Tiger chapter record a 'winch-mounted repeating crossbow', and a repeating crossbow has actually been unearthed from a Chu tomb of the Warring States. The Qin trigger mechanism kept its form into the Han and later, and the principle of firing in sequence survived in folk devices and in bed crossbows. Set in the Jiangnan of the ninth year of Daye, however, this weapon was not part of the insurgents' equipment. The rebels gathered at Wu and Piling with old-fashioned arms - bows, spears, shields and billhooks - and their siege methods were scaling ladders and mining, while their defence rested on numbers and on the archers and crossbowmen on the wall. The government troops had no repeating crossbow either: the walls of Wu and Danyang carried bed crossbows and crossbow artillery, backed by caltrops, abatis, log rollers and stone-throwers, and the besiegers answered with siege towers, battering carts, tunneling carts and fire-arrows. The only later age in which this sort of sequential firing became a service arm was the repeating crossbow of the Three Kingdoms and after; the Ming technical compendium Tiangong Kaiwu judged it that 'though the mechanism is ingenious, its power is feeble, it reaches only twenty-odd paces, and it is a household weapon for guarding against thieves, not a weapon of the state', while the Wubeizhi says that the people of the south-east like it for its lightness, that one crossbow looses ten bolts in succession, and that even cowards and housewives can hold one to guard a city. That is exactly the promise the card makes - the defenders keep the attackers pinned outside the wall - and it is technically achievable, yet in the fighting of 613 it remained a matter of the device rather than of battle: it never became something an army could rely on. The rivers and canals of Jiangnan made boats the normal means of supply for both sides; the Sui marched across the river from Jiangdu, and the insurgents moved north to Jian'an and back again to Wu by the waterways of Wu and the eastern Zhejiang.
tactics: 起義方採取的是典型的郡縣蜂起與合流進逼：七月劉元進先起於餘杭，旬月聚眾數萬，擬趁楊玄感在西線牽制、隋軍主力未返之際渡江北進；楊玄感很快敗亡，渡江之議遂罷，朱燮與管崇改為在江南內部會合，於吳郡一帶集兵並推出共主，隨後分頭響應，使毗陵、東陽、會稽、建安同時舉事，形成多點齊發、互為犄角的局面。攻城戰是義軍最弱的一環：十二月進攻丹陽，靠的是雲梯穴地這類簡陋手段，士卒缺乏編制與配合，器械與糧秣都靠就地徵發；隋將吐萬緒與魚俱羅率郡兵自丹陽正面抵擋，義軍久攻不克而士氣先竭，撤退時在黃山遭追擊截斷，管崇被斬，朱燮與劉元進僅以身免。退保建安之後，義軍沿途吸收新附之眾，再度折返吳郡重攻，這次卻遇上江都郡丞王世充以江南兵數萬渡江直趨城下，孤軍深入、糧援斷絕，最終在吳郡城下崩潰。官軍的戰術重點不在斬首，而在分割與殲滅：以中樞郡兵守住丹陽等城池，把義軍釘在城下，再以追擊打其退路，最後由王世充的水陸大軍收網圍攻吳郡，殲其主力。若說這場戰爭裡有過連發弩的影子，也只停留在城頭守禦的層面：義軍若得床弩一類器械，頂多在城外結陣壓制城頭射界，難以扭攻城頭與攻城者之間的火力落差。
tacticsEn: The insurgents used the classic pattern of a rising that starts in several commanderies at once and then converges for a combined advance. Liu Yuanjin rose first at Yuhang in the seventh month, drew tens of thousands within a month, and meant to cross the river and march north while Yang Xiangan held the western front and the main Sui army had not yet come back. Yang's revolt was crushed almost at once, and the project of crossing was abandoned. Zhu Xie and Guan Chong therefore turned to convergence inside Jiangnan, mustering at Wu, putting forward a common sovereign, and then setting off separate risings so that Piling, Dongyang, Kuaiji and Jian'an all rose in the same breath, many points flaring at once and supporting one another. Siege was the weakest part of the rebel army. The attack on Danyang in the twelfth month relied on crude means, scaling ladders and mining; the men had neither drill nor coordination, and both their equipment and their food were taken on the spot. Tu Wanzu and Fish Julu met them head on from Danyang with the commandery militia, the attack pined out and the rebels' morale broke first, and the retreat was cut off at Huangshan, where Guan Chong was beheaded and only Liu Yuanjin and Zhu Xie escaped with their lives. After falling back on Jian'an, the insurgents absorbed fresh followers on the road and turned once more to attack Wu; this time Wang Shichong, deputy prefect of Jiangdu, took several tens of thousands of Jiangnan troops across the river and drove straight at the city, and the rebels, isolated and cut off from supplies, collapsed beneath its walls. The Sui plan was not to seize leaders but to divide and then annihilate: hold the central cities such as Danyang with the commandery militia, pin the insurgents under them, cut their line of retreat in pursuit, and finally close the net around Wu with Wang Shichong's army moving by land and water. If the repeating crossbow played any part in this war, it was only in the defensive layer: had the rebels possessed bed crossbows they might at most have formed up outside the walls and pressed the firing lines of the defenders, but they could not have reversed the fire gap between the ramparts and the men scaling them.
data: 可核的數字集中在時間、兵員與折損三組。時間上，大業九年七月起兵，十二月即在丹陽受挫，吳郡決戰仍在同一年之內，從起事到全軍覆滅不足半年。兵員上，劉元進初起旬月眾至數萬，朱燮與管崇合兵後擁眾七萬，毗陵、東陽、會稽、建安各有眾響應；官軍方面，吐萬緒以左屯衛大將軍之眾偕光祿大夫魚俱羅下江南，另有王世充自江都發江南兵數萬渡江。折損上，《隋書》朱燮一節記丹陽之敗戰死五千兵馬，劉元進、朱燮僅以身免；其後吳郡之役兵敗，兩人戰死，降卒三萬餘人被坑殺於黃亭澗。地理上，吳郡為起義核心，即今江蘇蘇州；毗陵在吳郡西北，今江蘇常州；丹陽即隋丹陽郡治曲阿，在吳郡以西、今江蘇丹陽一帶；建安在今福建建甌，隔浙嶺而守。吳郡至丹陽、至毗陵均在百里上下，江南水網縱橫，官軍渡江與義軍轉戰多仰賴舟船，這一點也說明大隊一旦離開水路，補給極為脆弱。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked fall into three groups: time, numbers and losses. On time, the rising began in the seventh month of the ninth year of Daye, the army was checked at Danyang in the twelfth, and the decisive battle at Wu was fought within the same year, so the whole affair lasted less than half a year from outbreak to annihilation. On numbers, Liu Yuanjin drew tens of thousands within a month of his first rising, Zhu Xie and Guan Chong mustered seventy thousand between them once merged, and Piling, Dongyang, Kuaiji and Jian'an each answered with crowds of their own; on the government side, Tu Wanzu came south with his troops as Left Commandery Protector General, accompanied by Fish Julu, and Wang Shichong crossed the river from Jiangdu with several tens of thousands of Jiangnan soldiers. On losses, the chapter on Zhu Xie in the History of Sui records that five thousand men were lost at Danyang and that Liu Yuanjin and Zhu Xie escaped with nothing but their lives; after the defeat at Wu both men were killed, and more than thirty thousand men who had surrendered were put to death at Huangting Brook. On geography, Wu Commandery, the centre of the rising, is present-day Suzhou in Jiangsu; Piling lies to the northwest and is present-day Changzhou; Danyang, the seat of the Sui Danyang commandery at Qua, lies west of Wu in what is now Danyang county in Jiangsu; Jian'an, the place to which the rebels withdrew, is present-day Jian'ou in Fujian, held across the Zhejiang mountains. Both Danyang and Piling lie within a hundred li of Wu. The rivers and canals of Jiangnan made boats the usual means of movement for the Sui crossing the river and for the insurgents on their turnings, and that is precisely why a large force cut off from the waterways found its supply extremely fragile.
cause: 大業九年之前，隋朝已把江南的膏血耗到極處。煬帝連年東征高句麗，役繁力竭，吳、會一帶的士卒多已逃亡，民間對徵役的怨望達到頂點，士卒的怨言說得直白：去年跟著皇帝出征的父兄，即使在軍容最盛之時也已死亡大半，骸骨都沒能回鄉，如今天下已罷敝，再徵恐怕連剩下的都難保。七月，禮部尚書楊玄感在黎陽起兵反隋，天下響應，隋軍主力被牽制在北方，江淮一線兵力空虛，這是直接的時間窗口。吳郡的朱燮、毗陵的管崇正是在這個空檔裡起兵：朱燮以縣博士之身聚學生起事，憑的是通經史、習兵法的學力與士紳的號召；餘杭劉元進那邊好俠之風尚存，起事很快得到響應。江南是隋的漕運倉廩與賦稅根柢，郡兵多為臨時徵發、訓練不足，中央對吳郡、丹陽、江都的控制只剩下一層城防與一紙黃籍，稅糧一斷，秩序立刻崩落。於是三支互不相識的起義兵在半年之內同時舉事，說明隋朝在江南的統治基座已從根部斷裂，起義並非偶發的治安事件，而是整個體制的崩解徵候。
causeEn: Before the ninth year of Daye the Sui had drained the fat of Jiangnan to the last drop. The emperor had campaigned against Goguryeo year upon year, the corvee grew unbearable, and in the districts of Wu and Kuaiji the conscripts were fleeing in numbers; resentment of the levy reached its height, and the soldiers said it plainly: of those who went with the emperor last year, even at the height of the army's strength more than half are dead and their bones never came home; now the realm is exhausted, and if we are levied again perhaps not one of us will be left. In the seventh month Yang Xiangan, minister of rites, raised revolt at Liyang; the whole empire answered, the main Sui army was pinned in the north, and the Yangtze-Huai line was stripped of troops. That was the immediate opening. Zhu Xie of Wu and Guan Chong of Piling rose precisely in that gap: Zhu Xie, a county school official, gathered his students and rose on the strength of his learning in the classics and the art of war and on the pull of the local gentry, while in Yuhang the old chivalrous temper of Liu Yuanjin answered the call without delay. Jiangnan was the Sui's granary and its tax base; the commandery militia were hastily conscripted and poorly trained; and the court's hold over Wu, Danyang and Jiangdu had come down to a single line of city walls and a single yellow register. Once the tax grain failed, order collapsed at once. That three unrelated risings should break out within half a year showed that the Sui's footing in Jiangnan had cracked at the root, and that the rising was not an isolated disturbance of public order but a symptom of the coming collapse of the whole system.
impact: 朱燮起義是隋末民變在江南的第一聲，它的直接後果是隋廷被迫把兵力的重心在東征與平叛之間反覆調動，攻打高句麗的計劃因此一再押後，江南的漕運與糧秣又一次被臨時徵發，加劇了本已枯竭的民力。更大的影響在次序與示範：起義眾旬月集數萬、兩部合流即擁眾七萬、五個月之內轉戰吳越千里，證明鄉里的抗役網絡可以在沒有軍械與糧秣的情況下迅速變成軍隊，江南的郡兵與城防不再被視為不可動搖的屏障。一年之後，吳郡、丹陽一帶又出現規模更大的起義，沈法興、汪文進等相繼據城自立，隋朝只能靠王世充這些兼領地方兵權的官員勉力維持，江都的守成其實已經寄於一人的私兵與威望。大業十四年（618）煬帝遇弒，619 年王世充廢楊侑，隋室名號僅存空殼；此役之後江南再未真正恢復，政權先後落入沈法興、李子通、汪華、杜伏威與唐軍之手，戰亂延續到唐武德年間。對後世而言，朱燮這類以學官、以士紳、以一句「民苦役者，赴之為歸」號召流民的起義，成為唐宋以下鄉社起義書寫中最常被引用的原型之一，其名號雖在當時即被剿滅，其示範卻一直留在江南的記憶裡。
impactEn: The rising of Zhu Xie was the first shot fired in the Jiangnan uprisings of the late Sui, and its immediate consequence was that the court was forced to shift the centre of its military effort back and forth between the eastern campaign and the suppression of rebellion; the planned invasion of Goguryeo was put off again and again, and the grain and transport of Jiangnan were requisitioned once more, deepening a shortage of manpower that was already severe. The larger effect lay in the pattern and the example: tens of thousands within a month, seventy thousand as soon as two forces merged, campaigns of a thousand li across Wu and Yue within five months - these showed that the network of villages resisting the levy could be turned into an army with no weapons and no stores, and that the commandery militia and the walled cities of Jiangnan could no longer be treated as barriers that could not be moved. A year later larger risings appeared around Wu and Danyang, with Shen Faxing, Wang Wenjin and others setting up in their own cities; the Sui could hold on only through officials such as Wang Shichong who combined civil office with local command, and the defence of Jiangdu in truth rested on one man's private troops and personal standing. In 618 Emperor Yang was killed, and in 619 Wang Shichong deposed Yang You: the Sui name survived as an empty shell. After this rising Jiangnan never truly recovered; authority passed in turn to Shen Faxing, Li Zitong, Wang Hua, Du Fuwei and finally to Tang troops, and the fighting continued into the Wude years of the Tang. For later ages, an uprising of the kind Zhu Xie led - by a school official, by the gentry, and with the call that those wearied by forced labour would find in him a way home - became one of the most frequently cited models in the writing of village uprisings from the Tang and Song onward; his name was wiped out within the year, but the example stayed in the memory of Jiangnan.
result: 以戰局論，朱燮這條線以徹底覆滅收場：管崇在黃山被斬，劉元進與朱燮在吳郡城下兵敗戰死，投降的三萬餘人被坑殺於黃亭澗，吳郡與毗陵的起義眾隨之潰散，煙塵在半年之內平定。以政治論，隋廷贏得了這場戰爭，卻輸掉了整個江南：吳郡雖重歸官軍之手，戶口、糧賦與鄉里對朝廷的信任並未回復，兩年後即有規模更大的起義接踵而至，隋朝本身也只剩兩年壽命。對朱燮本人而言，他以一個縣博士之身拉起數十名學生的隊伍，半年之間做到僕射、號令一方，最終戰死於他起兵的城，沒有留下可以延續的政權或建制；他留下的是一句被後世反覆引用的話——民苦役者，赴之為歸——以及一個用連發弩守住城頭的技術想像：真正能把攻城者壓在牆外的，從來不只是一件兵器，而是組織、糧秣與士氣跟不跟得上。
resultEn: In military terms, Zhu Xie's line ended in complete destruction: Guan Chong was beheaded at Huangshan, Liu Yuanjin and Zhu Xie were killed in the defeat beneath the walls of Wu, and the more than thirty thousand who surrendered were put to death at Huangting Brook, the crowds at Wu and Piling dispersing with them, the whole affair settled within half a year. In political terms, the Sui won the war and lost Jiangnan with it: although Wu came back into the hands of the government, neither the households, nor the taxes and grain, nor the countryside's trust in the court was restored, and within two years larger risings followed one another, while the Sui dynasty itself had only two years left to run. As for Zhu Xie himself, he began with a few dozen students from the position of a county school official, rose within half a year to a ministerial command over a region, and died under the walls of the city where he had raised his banner, leaving behind neither a state nor an establishment that could be carried on. What he left was a sentence that later ages have quoted again and again - those wearied by forced labour would find in him a way home - together with a technical imagining of the repeating crossbow holding the wall: what truly keeps the attacker pinned outside the wall has never been a single weapon, but whether organisation, supply and morale keep pace with it.
